title: Tunability of the structural and magnetic transition in kagome material: PrIr$_3$B$_2$
authors: Gayathri V, Irshad K A, Sathishkumar M, Boby Joseph, S. Manni
abstract: We report the temperature and pressure tunability of an unusual structural transformation associated with a two-step metal-insulator-metal (MIM) transition in the kagome lattice compound PrIr$_3$B$_2$ using synchrotron X-ray powder diffraction. At ambient conditions of temperature and pressure, the monoclinic ($C2/m$) and the hexagonal ($P6/mmm$) phases coexist as twinned structure in the crystal. As the temperature (pressure) is decreased (increased), PrIr$_3$B$_2$ converts fully to monoclinic structure at $T =$ 280 K (at ambient pressure) and $P =$ 1.2 GPa (at room temperature). Temperature dependence of the monoclinic structure at ambient pressure presents complex evolution of lattice parameters with weak but clearly discernable anomalies at \SI{\sim 250} {\K} and \SI{\sim 110} {\K}, which are correlated with the second MIM transition and the linear to nonlinear temperature-dependent resistivity crossover, respectively. These anomalies are likely due to some charge order state causing a partially gapped Fermi surface. The magnetic phase diagram of PrIr$_3$B$_2$ is also investigated from anisotropic measurements. At 10 K, a superzone gap opens near the antiferromagnetic transition, which does not close even in the polarized state. From the tunability of the crystal structure and magnetic and electronic ground state, promising electronic orders are indicated in this kagome metallic magnet.
summary: This work reports on the structural and electronic phase diagram of the kagome magnet PrIr3B2, revealing a structural transition at 280 K correlated with a two-step metal-insulator-metal transition. Using XRD, resistivity, and magnetic measurements, the study suggests that charge ordering plays a crucial role in stabilizing these complex electronic and structural ground states.
main_problem: The study investigates the temperature and pressure tunability of structural transformations and associated two-step metal-insulator-metal (MIM) transitions in the kagome lattice compound PrIr3B2.
main_result: The compound undergoes a structural transition from hexagonal to monoclinic phase at T = 280 K (ambient pressure), which correlates with an anomalous two-step MIM transition and suggests the presence of charge order states.
method: The research employs synchrotron X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) to track structural changes under varying temperature and pressure, complemented by electrical resistivity and DSC measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is PrIr3B2, a kagome lattice magnet, whose electronic and structural ground states are being mapped out by observing transitions between different crystalline phases.
key_observables: Structural phases (monoclinic vs. hexagonal), two-step MIM transition in resistivity, lattice parameters (a, b, c), and magnetic susceptibility/heat capacity.
important_parameters: Temperature (T), Pressure (P), and magnetic field strength (H). Key transitions occur around 280 K and 110 K.
main_assumptions: The observed anomalies are hypothesized to be due to a charge order state causing a partially gapped Fermi surface, although the exact mechanism remains unclear.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD patterns tracking structural phase changes with T and P; resistivity plots highlight the two-step MIM transition; DSC curves reveal thermal events.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes structural transitions using XRD under T and P variations, correlates these structural changes with electronic transitions observed via resistivity measurements, and investigates the magnetic response using magnetization and heat capacity measurements.
why_interesting: The strong coupling observed between structural transitions, electronic transitions (MIM), and magnetic ordering in a correlated material like PrIr3B2 provides a rich playground for understanding emergent quantum phases in strongly correlated electron systems.
